text: Be yourself; everyone else is already taken.
author: Oscar Wilde
note: ATTRIBUTION DISPUTED. Universally credited to Wilde; not found in any of his published works, letters or recorded conversation. First traced to the late 20th century. This is the site's motto — decide whether to keep it attributed, run it unattributed as a phrase, or retire it.

text: We are all in the gutter, but some of us are looking at the stars.
author: Oscar Wilde

text: A cynic is a man who knows the price of everything and the value of nothing.
author: Oscar Wilde

text: The truth is rarely pure and never simple.
author: Oscar Wilde
source: The Importance of Being Earnest, Act I

text: Price is nothing. Value is everything.
Well done is better than well said.
author: Benjamin Franklin

text: To be yourself in a world that is constantly trying to make you something else is the greatest accomplishment.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
note: ATTRIBUTION DISPUTED. Universally credited to Emerson; not found in his published works. Also circulates as e.e. cummings. No primary source.

text: Live in the sunshine, swim the sea, drink the wild air.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

text: What you do speaks so loudly that I cannot hear what you say.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

text: Nothing great was ever achieved without enthusiasm.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

text: The greater danger for most of us lies not in setting our aim too high and falling short, but in setting our aim too low, and achieving our mark.
author: Michelangelo
note: ATTRIBUTION DISPUTED. No primary source in Michelangelo's letters or poems; appears to be 20th-century. Also the longest line here at 29 words.

text: In theory, there is no difference between theory and practice. But in practice, there is.
author: Yogi Berra
note: Attributed to Berra, but also to Van de Snepscheut and others. No primary source.

text: I find that the harder I work, the more luck I seem to have.
author: Thomas Jefferson
note: ATTRIBUTION DISPUTED. The Jefferson Foundation lists this as spurious — not found in his papers. Older versions run to Coleman Cox (1922).

text: Never interrupt your enemy when he is making a mistake.
author: Napoleon Bonaparte
note: ATTRIBUTION DISPUTED. Universally credited to Napoleon; no primary source in his correspondence.

text: Let us never negotiate out of fear. But let us never fear to negotiate.
author: John F. Kennedy

text: History doesn't repeat itself, but it does rhyme.
author: Mark Twain
note: ATTRIBUTION DISPUTED. Not found in Twain. The Mark Twain Project lists it as unverified.

text: And, when you want something, all the universe conspires in helping you to achieve it.
author: Paulo Coelho

text: The fool doth think he is wise, but the wise man knows himself to be a fool.
author: William Shakespeare
source: As You Like It, Act V

text: Every life is in many days, day after day. We walk through ourselves, meeting robbers, ghosts, giants, old men, young men, wives, widows, brothers-in-love, but always meeting ourselves.
author: James Joyce

text: You miss 100% of the shots you don't take.
author: Wayne Gretzky

text: The best way to predict the future is to create it.
author: Peter Drucker
note: ATTRIBUTION DISPUTED. The sourced version is Alan Kay, 1971: "The best way to predict the future is to invent it." Drucker attribution has no primary source.

text: You either die a hero or live long enough to see yourself become the villain.
author: Harvey Dent
note: Fictional — screenplay by Jonathan and Christopher Nolan. Attributed to the character, which is the honest way to run it.

text: Just win, baby
author: Al Davis

text: Perhaps one did not want to be loved so much as to be understood.
author: George Orwell

text: He who dares not offend cannot be honest.
author: Thomas Paine
note: Attributed to Paine. Widely cited, primary source not confirmed.

text: The most valuable of all talents is that of never using two words when one will do.
author: Thomas Jefferson

text: It is easier to do a job right than to explain why you didn't.
author: Martin Van Buren
note: ATTRIBUTION DISPUTED. No primary source in Van Buren's papers.

text: Everyone has a plan until they get punched in the mouth.
author: Mike Tyson

text: There is only one thing in the world worse than being talked about, and that is not being talked about.
author: Oscar Wilde

text: We are all apprentices in a craft where no one ever becomes a master.
author: Ernest Hemingway
note: Attributed to Hemingway, widely. No primary source located.

text: Everyone thinks of changing the world, but no one thinks of changing himself.
author: Leo Tolstoy

text: It ain't what you don't know that gets you into trouble. It's what you know for sure that just ain't so.
author: Mark Twain
note: ATTRIBUTION DISPUTED. Not Twain — traces to Josh Billings. The Mark Twain Project lists it as unverified.

text: The cure for anything is salt water: sweat, tears, or the sea.
author: Isak Dinesen
note: Attributed to Dinesen; not located in Seven Gothic Tales or her letters.

text: Not everything that can be counted counts, and not everything that counts can be counted.
author: William Bruce Cameron

text: We suffer more often in imagination than in reality.
author: Seneca

text: It's only when the tide goes out that you learn who has been swimming naked.
author: Warren Buffett

text: Either write something worth reading or do something worth writing.
author: Benjamin Franklin

text: Show me the incentive and I will show you the outcome.
author: Charlie Munger

text: The best victory is that which requires no battle.
author: Sun Tzu

text: The medium is the message.
author: Marshall McLuhan

text: Do what you can, with what you have, where you are.
author: Theodore Roosevelt
note: Roosevelt quoted it in his Autobiography (1913), crediting Squire Bill Widener. Not original to him.

text: It does not matter how slowly you go as long as you do not stop.
author: Confucius
note: ATTRIBUTION DISPUTED. Not in the Analects. Modern Western invention.

text: Positive anything is better than negative nothing.
author: Elbert Hubbard
